title.narrative: Number of national strategies and programmes implemented addressing specific rights/concerns of IPs

description.narrative: Number of national strategies and programmes implemented addressing specific rights/concerns of IPs

comment.narrative: Bangladesh Ministry of Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs developed their SDG implementation plan. Nepal Indigenous community and local government members built a common understanding on indigenous peoples rights and development. Cambodia Engagements with the government were intensified despite a not so supportive political environment and the member of the local partner have strengthened their advocacy with the government by monitoring public policies. Philippines Commission on Human Rights is establishing an Indigenous Peoples Human Rights Observatory and assurances have been provided that the Navigator tools will be adopted for its database. Tanzania Where government permission was required to undertake data collection the National Bureau of Statistics granted the legal permit for conducting the surveys for data gathering in the project areas. Kenya Consultations among indigenous peoples ILOs social partners and government agencies on climate change and green jobs resulted in a draft project architecture that includes the Navigator as a tool for data.Cameroon Results of data collection were shared with the Cameroonian National Statistics Bureau and there was a broad agreement on the need for disaggregated data on the situation of indigenous peoples.Suriname National Statistics Bureau has expressed interest in the collection of disaggregated data on indigenous peoples with regard to the SDGs.
In 11 focus countries progress has been made in national policies relating to SDGs and IPs building on the achievements of the previous phases of the Initiative.

title.narrative: Ensure the sustainability of the Indigenous Navigator Initiative

description.narrative: The present Action aims to ensure the sustainability of the Indigenous Navigator Initiative both in terms of increased local resource mobilisation of the national partners, as well as institutional and technical development and the continued operation of the portal, which is freely accessible, and used worldwide. Moreover, the Action will support international advocacy and build alliances with strategic partners within the human rights and sustainable development field, accountability of dutybearers visvis rights holders.
